newsitem.title: USA: Now a primary dealer, Paribas eyes breaking top 10.
newsitem.headline: Now a primary dealer, Paribas eyes breaking top 10.

text.p: Now that Paribas Corp has been added to the U.S. primary dealer ranks, the firm has set its sights on becoming a major force in the U.S. government securities business.
"We don't want to be just the 38th primary dealer, we want to be in the top 10," said a top Paribas official in New York.

He noted that since the top "five to seven (dealers) run the (government bond) business quite actively," Paribas is not looking to unseat them. "But we would like to reach the top 10," the official, who declined to be named, said in an interview with Reuters.

Paribas currently has 10 government bond traders and seven salesmen in New York, up from a desk of two just a few years ago, according to the company. And the firm said that its New York expansion in fixed income should take another 18 months.
The official said Paribas, which became a primary dealer on Thursday, has worked on gaining primary dealer status for some time.

Paribas is currently the 38th primary dealer, and becomes the first 100 percent French-owned primary dealer. The firm is the first to join the dealer ranks since CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp in early 1996, according to the New York Fed.

In recent years the number of primary dealers, which are counterparties to the Federal Reserve, has dwindled -- mainly due to mergers between firms such as Manufacturers Hanover Bank and Chemical Bank and then Chemical and Chase Manhattan Bank, PaineWebber and Kidder Peabody, and S.G. Warburg and Swiss Bank Corp.
The soon-to-be completed deal between Dean Witter Reynolds and Morgan Stanley, and analysts' expectations of further mergers, will whittle that number down further.
The Paribas official said the company was always interested in penetrating the U.S. market, especially since it has done well in Asia and Europe.
He said a significant U.S. government bond desk will add to its existing products of swaps, derivatives, emerging markets, foreign equities, Yankees and Eurodollars.
Plus, he said, Paribas in New York looks to grow in corporate bonds and high yield and do more underwriting.
Paribas Corp is the U.S. registered broker/dealer affiliate of Paribas, an international investment bank.
